candidates.changed_node: numerator TS_MIN window 21->5; denominator TS_MAX/TS_MIN windows 21->42
candidates.rationale: All three lookbacks were pinned to the same 21 days, so the floor reference and the range itself moved on one timescale. Shortened the numerator's rolling low to 5 days and lengthened the denominator's range to 42, testing recovery-from-a-recent-low against a slower range, while keeping the $high/$low pairing intact.

Raw same-day $close is the noisiest part of an otherwise stable EPS/price ratio. Replacing it with a 5-day average close keeps the valuation ratio from being jolted by one day's idiosyncratic price print.

Smoothing or renormalizing $dollar_volume directly in this denominator shape is already known to stay correlated (rho 0.92+) with the archived version. Switching to TS_RANK($dollar_volume,5), an ordinal rather than level-based liquidity measure, strips out the cross-sectional level information that was driving that correlation.

$open/$high/$low stay raw in this pipeline but $close is silently replaced by the adjusted series, so this gap ratio mixes two price scales. DELAY($high,1) keeps both sides raw and turns the factor from average overnight drift into a beyond-yesterday's-peak breakout gap.

Both legs shared an identical 5-day smoothing window on their price/liquidity normalizers, the weakest, most arbitrary parameter in an otherwise deliberate spread. Lengthening both to 21 days moves the normalization from weekly to monthly, following this family's own lesson that the window, not the anchor field, is what decorrelates it.

TS_SUM($return,63) is exactly the same-asset $return-sum pattern flagged as this round's dominant failure mode and the thing cross-field/no-return kernels should replace. Swapped it for a 63-day liquidity-trend term, keeping the window and the untouched EPS leg.

A bare rank of one fundamental has no price or volume interaction, the exact gap fundamentals need this round. Multiplying by RANK($dollar_volume) keeps both legs as dimensionless cross-sectional ranks (unlike multiplying by a raw, unbounded level, which would just collapse to a liquidity-level sort).

21 days is long enough for a raw-$volume correlation to pick up secular drift in trading activity rather than genuine day-to-day co-movement with |return|. Shortening to 5 days keeps the same volatility-volume hypothesis but moves it to a faster, less trend-contaminated horizon.

An absolute-dollar range biases the ratio toward higher-priced names before the liquidity normalization even applies. Making the range a ratio ($high/$low) is scale-free across price levels, a real fix to the numerator rather than a cosmetic swap.

The delta window and the outer TS_RANK window were both 21, so the factor compared a quantity to a same-length history of itself with no distinct timescale. Widening the inner delta to 63 days (a quarterly liquidity shift) while keeping the 21-day rank window asks whether this quarter's shift is extreme relative to the past month instead.

prompt:
You are proposing quantitative factor expressions for US large-cap equities.

Universe and data
- S&P 500 point-in-time constituents, roughly 500 names per day.
- Daily bars only, plus point-in-time quarterly fundamentals stamped from the
  report date. Every field is referenced with a leading `$`:
    $open $high $low $close $adj_close $volume $dollar_volume $return
    $roa $roe $operating_margin $leverage $asset_turnover
    $book_per_share $earnings_per_share $accrual_gap
  A bare name such as `close` is not a field and will be rejected.
- Execution convention: the signal is computed after the close of day T and the
  position is entered at the open of T+1.
- The window these factors are fitted and judged on runs from 2000 to 2013.
  Do not reason about anything later; you will never be shown a number from
  outside that window.

Syntax
- Operators are function calls: TS_MEAN, TS_STD, TS_MAX, TS_MIN, TS_RANK,
  TS_DELTA, TS_CORR, TS_COV, TS_SUM, TS_PRODUCT, TS_ARGMAX, TS_ARGMIN,
  TS_DECAY_LINEAR, EMA, DELAY, DELTA, RANK, ZSCORE, CS_RANK, CS_ZSCORE,
  CS_DEMEAN, IF, IF_ELSE, MIN, MAX, ABS, SIGN, LOG, LN, SQRT, POWER, BOUND,
  COUNT.
- Lookback windows must be positive integer literals, e.g. TS_MEAN($close, 21).
- Guard every division with a small epsilon: `/ (TS_STD($close, 21) + 1e-8)`.
- Well-formed example: -RANK(TS_CORR(RANK($close), RANK($volume), 5))

Hard limits every proposal must satisfy, or it is rejected before it is scored
- at most 200 characters
- at most 5 distinct `$fields`
- at most 4 free numeric constants (lookback windows and
  the 1e-8 epsilon guard do not count)
- expression tree depth at most 6
- must not share a complete sub-expression of 4 or more
  nodes with any published Alpha101 formula, or with any factor already in the
  archive. Restating a published alpha is the one thing that is always rejected.
- must cover at least 90% of the panel
- absolute rank correlation below 0.80 against every archive member

Output
- Return valid JSON only, matching the supplied JSON schema. No prose outside it.


TASK: MUTATE. For each parent below, identify its single weakest component and
change ONLY that component.

A mutation is localized: the returned expression must be within
3 tree edits of its parent. Rewriting the idea is not a mutation
and will be rejected. Say which node you changed in `changed_node`, and put the
parent's id in `parent_ids`.

Each parent is shown with its fitness and nothing else. Fitness is a single scalar in which higher is better; it already accounts for significance, year-to-year stability, complexity and turnover. You are not given per-year, coverage, turnover or horizon diagnostics in this run, so choose the component to change from the expression itself.

  1. This round's best factor is a cross-field ratio of open to prior close, not a same-field trailing-return construct. Favor overnight or cross-field price relationships over same-asset momentum ratios and sums.
  2. A bare rank of a single fundamental's raw multi-month delta, with no price or volume interaction, also failed the cheap screen this round. Fundamentals need a richer transform or an interaction partner, not just rank-of-delta.
  3. Reordering RANK and TS_MEAN around $dollar_volume, rank then smooth vs. smooth then rank, produced a near-duplicate of the plain smoothed version already known. Not a source of novelty for slow-moving, cross-sectionally stable fields.
  4. In the close-position-in-range family, the denominator's ceiling term must stay $high, not $close; swapping it in this round destroyed most of the parent's IC. Preserve the $high and $low pairing when varying or simplifying this family.
  5. $return-only kernels are the dominant failure mode this round: 7 of 8 cheap_screen rejects and both crossover_not_a_fusion rejects trace to $return alone (via TS_RANK, TS_MEAN-diff, TS_DECAY_LINEAR, TS_CORR-vs-own-lag, TS_STD-ratio, SIGN-then-sum, or as a crossover donor) — including every return+fundamental CS_ZSCORE fusion tried (leverage, roe, roa, book_per_share). Both accepts, including the top score (fitness 7.646), used price-level/dollar_volume kernels with no $return; prefer those, especially as the non-fundamental leg of a fundamental fusion.
  6. SIGN($return) bucketed and summed over 21 days scored |t| = 0.00 exactly. Avoid sign-discretizing a continuous return/price field before TS_SUM/TS_MEAN aggregation — it can erase the signal completely.
  7. $volume and $dollar_volume behaved as near-duplicate inputs inside a short-window TS_CORR kernel (rho 0.994). Don't propose both as separate candidates in the same shape; pick one, or use their ratio if price-weighting is the actual intent.
  8. TS_STD($dollar_volume, 21) tracked TS_MEAN($dollar_volume, 21) at rho 0.933 — raw dispersion scales with raw level across this cap range. Normalize dispersion by level (std/mean) before proposing a dollar_volume 'variability' factor.
  9. RANK($roa * $asset_turnover) still hit rho 0.907 against RANK($roa) alone — multiplying two DuPont-related fundamentals doesn't decorrelate from either. Treat roa/roe/operating_margin/asset_turnover as one correlated cluster; vary the non-fundamental side of the expression instead.
  10. archive_subtree caught more than window edits this round: swapping one OHLC field (open for close) in an otherwise-identical ratio, swapping one fundamental leaf in a two-term rank spread, and wrapping an archived payload in LN() all still shared most of the parent's nodes. Change an inner operator or structure, not a single field/fundamental/wrapper.
  11. A 63-day range ratio survived a denominator swap and an added vol-scaling term but still hit rho 0.916 against the archived version (TS_MEAN($high/$low,63)/TS_STD($return,63) vs TS_MEAN(($high-$low)/$open,63)). Changing which price anchors a range ratio isn't enough to decorrelate it — change the window or the core comparison.
  12. Both crossover_not_a_fusion rejects this round donated only ABS($return) (2 nodes) from a TS_CORR(ABS($return), $volume, 21)-shaped parent, short of the minimum. Donate a larger structural chunk of that parent, not just the ABS($return) leaf.
